blocks.x: Golden paths turn engineering months into days — and make the secure path the easy path.

Why Platform engineering is the highest-draw on hire you will make: because the differentiated advantage has moved to the data layer and the operating model around it. The technology is the commodity; the discipline is the moat.

items: Backstage-class catalogs with scorecards make ownership visible and drift actionable.
DORA metrics belong on the platform team's roadmap, not just engineering's vanity dashboard.
Platform-as-product (roadmap, budget, NPS) separates adopted platforms from routed-around ones.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: Programs like Platform engineering is the highest-draw on hire you will make rarely fail on the technology. They fail on unnamed ownership, unmeasured baselines and ungated scope — the three failure modes the guards on this page are built for.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Paved-road services typically see lead time fall 50%+ with change-failure rate falling alongside.
Where this shows up in our work
